## 1. Introduction

This report explores the relationship between body mass
and flipper length in three Antarctic penguin species:
Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo.

The analysis demonstrates how to import data, clean
missing values, use a custom function, and visualize results.

## 2. Load packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

## 3. Import the data

The penguin dataset is stored as a CSV file in
the project's data folder.

```{r}
penguins <- read.csv("data/penguins.csv")

head(penguins)
```

## 4. Explore the original data

First, we examine the structure and dimensions of
the dataset.

```{r}
str(penguins)

dim(penguins)

summary(penguins)
```

### Check missing values

```{r}
colSums(is.na(penguins))
```

Some observations contain missing measurements.
For our analysis, we need body mass and flipper length.

## 5. Clean the data

We use a custom function stored in `R/functions.R`.

The function removes observations with missing body
mass or flipper length and converts body mass from
grams to kilograms.

```{r}
source("R/functions.R")

penguins_clean <- clean_penguins(penguins)

head(penguins_clean)
```

### Check the cleaning results

```{r}
nrow(penguins)

nrow(penguins_clean)

nrow(penguins) - nrow(penguins_clean)
```

The final calculation tells us how many observations
were removed during cleaning.

## 6. Create a figure

We investigate the relationship between flipper
length and body mass across penguin species.

```{r}
ggplot(
  penguins_clean,
  aes(
    x = flipper_len,
    y = body_mass_kg,
    color = species
  )
) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Penguin body mass vs flipper length",
    x = "Flipper length (mm)",
    y = "Body mass (kg)",
    color = "Penguin species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 7. Summary by species

We calculate the average body mass for each species.

```{r}
penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    mean_body_mass_kg = mean(body_mass_kg),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## 8. Conclusion

This analysis demonstrates a simple and reproducible
workflow for working with ecological data in R.

The data were imported, inspected, cleaned using a
custom function, and visualized with ggplot2.

The relationship between flipper length and body mass
can be compared among the three penguin species.
